## 1. Purpose of This Document

Per the STAT 663 Studio Threshold Requirements for **Reproducibility** and **Integrity** ("Preserve the first output of anything an assistant produced for you, with the prompt and date. Do not reprompt to obtain a more auditable failure"), this document records:

1.  **The Course AI Contribution Log** for the construction and statistical refinement of our Virginia Traffic Safety Executive R Shiny Dashboard.
2.  **The Exact Initial Prompt and Preserved First Output (`app.R` v1.0)** generated by Gemini Pro on November 10, 2026.
3.  **The Chronological Trail of Human Verification Checks, Defect Audits, and Revisions (Iterations 1–6)** showing what our human visual and statistical checks established, what failed in the AI's initial outputs, how we corrected each failure, and what residual concerns remain.
4.  **The Final Verified Dashboard Code (`app.R` v6.0)** shipped after human audit.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Combine M1/M2 prototype R scripts and Word outline into a 3-page executive R Shiny dashboard (First Output)** | Gemini Pro, 11/10/2026 | Generated initial 3-page `bslib` R Shiny dashboard (`app.R`) combining Page 1 county/weather summaries and `CIPI`/`CIPIrate`/`SARWC` plots, Page 2 county time-series and weather plots, and Page 3 Leaflet street map; fixed 0-accident months in conditional rates (`NA` instead of `0`) and matched counties by 5-digit Census `GEOID`. | Audited the rendered app in RStudio and identified four major visual, geospatial, and statistical defects requiring human revision across subsequent iterations (crowded error bars on bar charts, blank Leaflet map on rural counties, exploding `0–100%` CIs on Page 2 weather, and meaningless PIs). | Ran initial `app.R` against `Virginia_Accidents_With_Pop.csv`; verified timestamp parsing, `GEOID` joins, and reactivity across county tiers. | Initial output mixed point-estimate bars with error bars and failed on sparse county-weather-month combinations. |

Separate Confidence Intervals from top-row bar charts and adjust for multiple comparisons** | Gemini Pro, 11/10/2026 | Explained statistical and perceptual reasons why layering black Clopper-Pearson binomial CIs onto solid `ggplotly` bars crowded Page 1; removed `geom_errorbar()` from top-row bar charts on Pages 1 and 2, isolated intervals in dedicated panels, added Page 2 CI/PI panel, and added Bonferroni and Šidák FWER adjustments. | Directed the design rule that all CIs and PIs must be isolated in dedicated uncertainty charts rather than layered onto magnitude bar charts, and required family-wise error rate ($\text{FWER} = 5\%$) adjustments across simultaneous comparisons. | Visually verified in Shiny that top-row bar charts rendered cleanly without overlapping whiskers and checked that individual CI levels scaled dynamically as $1 - (0.05 / m)$. | Bonferroni adjustment is conservative when monthly weather or county series are correlated. |
| **3. Troubleshoot and fix Page 3 Leaflet map rendering blank on individual counties** | Gemini Pro, 11/10/2026 | Identified that `validate(need(nrow(streets_df) > 0))` wiped the entire map blank when rural counties had $<5$ accidents per street, that filtering out the other 132 counties removed statewide context, and that `CartoDB.Positron` tiles were washed out; updated code to always draw all 133 VA counties, use OpenStreetMap/Esri tiles, lock camera zoom via `fitBounds()`, and auto-fallback to `min = 1` street accident. | Tested individual counties on Page 3, caught that the map went blank and lost statewide Virginia context, and requested a real road map with statewide visibility and county click-to-zoom functionality. | Clicked through urban and rural Virginia counties in the live app to confirm the crimson county boundary, surrounding VA counties, street markers, and OpenStreetMap road network rendered without blanking out. | Street-level hotspot coordinates use the median GPS coordinate of accidents sharing a street name, which summarizes long interstates (e.g., I-95, I-81) as a single county centroid point. |
| **4. Diagnose and fix `0%` to `100%` exploding CIs and PIs for rare weather conditions on Page 2** | Gemini Pro, 11/10/2026 | Confirmed user's degrees-of-freedom diagnosis (rare weather strings like `"Heavy T-Storm / Windy"` occurred in only $N = 2$ or $3$ active months in a county, giving $\text{df} = 1$ or $2$ and Bonferroni $t$-critical values of $12.6$ to $101.8$, while 1-accident months created binary $0\%/100\%$ variance); proposed consolidating weather regimes and weighting monthly log-odds. | Audited Page 2 interval widths, identified the `0%–100%` anomaly on `"Heavy T-Storm / Windy"`, and diagnosed that rare weather conditions lacked sufficient active monthly observations ($\text{df}$) to support a monthly $t$-interval. | Inspected `N_Units` (active months) and CI bounds in the Page 2 `DT` table across multiple counties to verify that $\text{df}$ starvation was the root cause. | First logit transformation introduced a continuity-correction centering shift (`+ 0.5`) that required further human audit in Task 5. |
| **5. Audit one-sided CI bug and simplify Page 2 monthly weather CI methodology for executive interpretability** | Gemini Pro, 11/10/2026 | Identified that adding `+ 0.5` to monthly log-odds pulled small-count interval centers toward $50\%$ away from the pooled mean dot; replaced complex logit math with three plain-English rules using the textbook $\text{Mean} \pm t \cdot \text{SE}$ formula: (1) 5 Core Weather Categories, (2) $\ge 5$ accidents for a month to qualify, and (3) $\ge 10$ qualifying months ($\text{df} \ge 9$) per bar. | Caught visually that several CIs appeared one-sided around the point estimate; rejected black-box transformations and directed a simpler, transparent specification that an average policymaker can understand while guaranteeing sufficient $n$ per bar. | Verified that all red point-estimate dots sat strictly at the center of their symmetric $t$-intervals and that every plotted weather category had $n \ge 10$ qualifying months in major counties. | In very small rural counties with fewer total crashes, fallback thresholds ($\ge 2$ accidents/month, $\ge 3$ months) are triggered so the chart does not render empty. |

### First Output Code (`app.R` — Version 1.0, Preserved Verbatim)

```{r}

library(shiny)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. REPRODUCIBLE DATA LOADING & PREPROCESSING
# ==============================================================================
# Avoid hardcoded setwd() paths so the project runs from a clean checkout (M2/M4)
data_paths <- c(
  "../Data/Virginia_Accidents_With_Pop.csv",
  "Data/Virginia_Accidents_With_Pop.csv",
  "Virginia_Accidents_With_Pop.csv"
)

existing_path <- data_paths[file.exists(data_paths)][1]

if (is.na(existing_path)) {
  stop(
    "Data file 'Virginia_Accidents_With_Pop.csv' not found. ",
    "Ensure it is located in '../Data/' or 'Data/' relative to this script."
  )
}

# Read data; treat empty strings as NA so blank weather/street cells are caught
acc_raw <- read.csv(existing_path, na.strings = c("", "NA"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Clean and standardize variables
acc <- acc_raw %>%
  mutate(
    # Robust timestamp parsing (handles both ISO8601 'T/Z' and standard formats)
    Start_Time = ymd_hms(Start_Time, tz = "UTC", quiet = TRUE),
    End_Time   = ymd_hms(End_Time, tz = "UTC", quiet = TRUE),
    Year       = year(Start_Time),
    month_year = floor_date(Start_Time, unit = "month"),
    
    # Severity classification (Severity 3 & 4 = Severe)
    severe     = Severity >= 3,
    
    # Standardize GEOID as 5-character string for exact tigris spatial joins
    GEOID      = str_pad(as.character(GEOID), width = 5, side = "left", pad = "0"),
    
    # Clean text fields
    Weather_Condition = str_squish(Weather_Condition),
    Street            = str_squish(Street),
    census_name       = str_squish(census_name)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(census_name), !is.na(Severity), !is.na(Year))

# Pre-compute static county population rankings across all VA localities in data
county_pop_ranks <- acc %>%
  group_by(GEOID, census_name) %>%
  summarise(population = first( na.omit(population) ), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(population)) %>%
  mutate(pop_rank = row_number())

n_localities <- nrow(county_pop_ranks)
mid_start    <- max(1, floor((n_localities - 5) / 2) + 1)
mid_indices  <- mid_start:min(n_localities, mid_start + 4)

top5_pop_names    <- county_pop_ranks %>% slice_head(n = 5) %>% pull(census_name)
middle5_pop_names <- county_pop_ranks %>% slice(mid_indices) %>% pull(census_name)
bottom5_pop_names <- county_pop_ranks %>% slice_tail(n = 5) %>% pull(census_name)

all_years    <- sort(unique(acc$Year))
all_counties <- county_pop_ranks$census_name

# Load Virginia county/independent city boundaries once via tigris
va_boundaries <- tryCatch({
  counties(state = "VA", cb = TRUE, year = 2022, progress_bar = FALSE) %>%
    st_transform(4326)
}, error = function(e) {
  NULL
})

# Exact Clopper-Pearson 95% Binomial Confidence Interval helper (vectorized)
calc_binom_ci <- function(x, n, bound = c("lower", "upper")) {
  bound <- match.arg(bound)
  idx <- ifelse(bound == "lower", 1, 2)
  map2_dbl(x, n, function(k, total) {
    if (is.na(k) || is.na(total) || total <= 0) return(NA_real_)
    binom.test(k, total)$conf.int[idx]
  })
}

# Exact Garwood 95% Poisson Confidence Interval helper for monthly counts
calc_poisson_ci <- function(k_vec, bound = c("lower", "upper")) {
  bound <- match.arg(bound)
  idx <- ifelse(bound == "lower", 1, 2)
  map_dbl(k_vec, function(k) {
    if (is.na(k) || k < 0) return(NA_real_)
    poisson.test(as.integer(round(k)))$conf.int[idx]
  })
}

# ==============================================================================
# 3. SERVER LOGIC
# ==============================================================================
server <- function(input, output, session) {

  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # PAGE 1 REACTIVE DATA
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  p1_selected_counties <- reactive({
    switch(
      input$p1_pop_tier,
      "top5"  = top5_pop_names,
      "mid5"  = middle5_pop_names,
      "bot5"  = bottom5_pop_names,
      "top10" = county_pop_ranks %>% slice_head(n = 10) %>% pull(census_name),
      "all"   = all_counties
    )
  })

  p1_filtered_acc <- reactive({
    df <- acc %>% filter(census_name %in% p1_selected_counties())
    if (input$p1_year != "All") {
      df <- df %>% filter(Year == as.numeric(input$p1_year))
    }
    df
  })

  # County-level summary for Page 1
  p1_county_summary <- reactive({
    df <- p1_filtered_acc()
    
    # Keep all selected tier counties visible even if 0 accidents occurred in a given year
    base_counties <- county_pop_ranks %>%
      filter(census_name %in% p1_selected_counties())
    
    agg <- df %>%
      group_by(census_name) %>%
      summarise(
        total_accidents  = n(),
        severe_accidents = sum(severe, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
      )
    
    base_counties %>%
      left_join(agg, by = "census_name") %>%
      mutate(
        total_accidents  = replace_na(total_accidents, 0L),
        severe_accidents = replace_na(severe_accidents, 0L),
        severe_rate      = ifelse(total_accidents > 0, severe_accidents / total_accidents, 0),
        severe_ratio     = (severe_accidents / population) * 100000,
        rate_ci_low      = calc_binom_ci(severe_accidents, total_accidents, "lower"),
        rate_ci_high     = calc_binom_ci(severe_accidents, total_accidents, "upper")
      )
  })

  # KPI Outputs
  output$p1_kpi_total <- renderText({
    comma(sum(p1_county_summary()$total_accidents, na.rm = TRUE))
  })

  output$p1_kpi_rate <- renderText({
    tot_acc <- sum(p1_county_summary()$total_accidents, na.rm = TRUE)
    tot_sev <- sum(p1_county_summary()$severe_accidents, na.rm = TRUE)
    if (tot_acc == 0) return("0.0%")
    percent(tot_sev / tot_acc, accuracy = 0.1)
  })

  output$p1_kpi_ratio <- renderText({
    tot_pop <- sum(p1_county_summary()$population, na.rm = TRUE)
    tot_sev <- sum(p1_county_summary()$severe_accidents, na.rm = TRUE)
    if (tot_pop == 0) return("0.0")
    number((tot_sev / tot_pop) * 100000, accuracy = 0.1, big.mark = ",")
  })

  # Page 1 Plot 1: County Bar / Interval Chart
  output$p1_county_plot <- renderPlotly({
    df <- p1_county_summary()
    if (input$p1_pop_tier == "all") {
      df <- df %>% slice_max(.data[[input$p1_metric]], n = 15)
    }

    metric_label <- switch(
      input$p1_metric,
      "total_accidents" = "Total Recorded Accidents",
      "severe_rate"     = "Severe Accident Rate (% of County Accidents)",
      "severe_ratio"    = "Severe Accidents per 100,000 Residents"
    )

    p <- ggplot(
      df,
      aes(
        x = reorder(census_name, .data[[input$p1_metric]]),
        y = .data[[input$p1_metric]],
        text = paste0(
          "<b>", census_name, "</b><br>",
          "Population: ", comma(population), "<br>",
          "Total Accidents: ", comma(total_accidents), "<br>",
          "Severe Accidents: ", comma(severe_accidents), "<br>",
          "Severe Rate: ", percent(severe_rate, accuracy = 0.1), "<br>",
          "Severe Ratio (per 100k): ", round(severe_ratio, 1)
        )
      )
    ) +
      geom_col(fill = exec_navy, alpha = 0.9, width = 0.7)

    if (input$p1_metric == "severe_rate") {
      p <- p +
        geom_errorbar(
          aes(ymin = rate_ci_low, ymax = rate_ci_high),
          width = 0.25, color = exec_amber, linewidth = 0.8
        ) +
        scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format())
    } else {
      p <- p + scale_y_continuous(labels = comma_format())
    }

    p <- p +
      coord_flip() +
      labs(x = NULL, y = metric_label) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
      theme(
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#1A202C")
      )

    ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text") %>%
      config(displayModeBar = FALSE)
  })

  # Page 1 Plot 2: Weather Conditions Associated with Severe Accidents
  p1_weather_summary <- reactive({
    df <- p1_filtered_acc() %>%
      filter(!is.na(Weather_Condition), Weather_Condition != "") %>%
      group_by(Weather_Condition) %>%
      summarise(
        total_accidents  = n(),
        severe_accidents = sum(severe, na.rm = TRUE),
        severe_percent   = severe_accidents / total_accidents,
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      filter(total_accidents >= input$p1_min_weather_n) %>%
      slice_max(severe_percent, n = 10) %>%
      mutate(
        lower_ci = calc_binom_ci(severe_accidents, total_accidents, "lower"),
        upper_ci = calc_binom_ci(severe_accidents, total_accidents, "upper")
      )
    df
  })

  output$p1_weather_plot <- renderPlotly({
    df <- p1_weather_summary()
    validate(
      need(nrow(df) > 0, "No weather conditions meet the minimum accident count threshold for this selection. Lower the threshold slider.")
    )

    p <- ggplot(
      df,
      aes(
        x = reorder(Weather_Condition, severe_percent),
        y = severe_percent,
        text = paste0(
          "<b>", Weather_Condition, "</b><br>",
          "Severe Rate: ", percent(severe_percent, accuracy = 0.1), "<br>",
          "95% Binomial CI: [", percent(lower_ci, accuracy = 0.1), ", ",
          percent(upper_ci, accuracy = 0.1), "]<br>",
          "Severe / Total: ", comma(severe_accidents), " / ", comma(total_accidents)
        )
      )
    ) +
      geom_col(fill = exec_teal, alpha = 0.85, width = 0.65) +
      geom_errorbar(
        aes(ymin = lower_ci, ymax = upper_ci),
        width = 0.25, color = "#1A202C", linewidth = 0.7
      ) +
      coord_flip() +
      scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
      labs(
        x = NULL,
        y = "Severe Accidents (% of Total in Weather Condition)"
      ) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
      theme(
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold")
      )

    ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text") %>%
      config(displayModeBar = FALSE)
  })

  # Page 1 Plot 3 & Table: Grouped CIs (CIPI, CIPIrate, SARWC)
  p1_monthly_variance <- reactive({
    df <- p1_filtered_acc() %>% filter(!is.na(month_year))
    validate(need(nrow(df) > 0, "No monthly records available for this filter selection."))

    # Expand across the observed monthly sequence in the filtered data
    all_months <- seq(min(df$month_year), max(df$month_year), by = "1 month")

    monthly <- df %>%
      group_by(census_name, month_year) %>%
      summarise(
        severe_accidents = sum(severe, na.rm = TRUE),
        accidents        = n(),
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      complete(
        census_name = p1_selected_counties(),
        month_year  = all_months,
        fill = list(severe_accidents = 0L, accidents = 0L)
      ) %>%
      left_join(county_pop_ranks %>% select(census_name, population), by = "census_name") %>%
      mutate(
        # Per-capita ratio is validly 0 when 0 severe accidents occur in a month
        severe_ratio = (severe_accidents / population) * 100000,
        # Statistical Correction: Conditional rate P(Severe | Accident) is NA (not 0) when 0 accidents occur
        severe_rate  = ifelse(accidents == 0, NA_real_, severe_accidents / accidents)
      )
    monthly
  })

  p1_ci_data <- reactive({
    if (input$p1_ci_type == "SARWC") {
      df <- p1_weather_summary() %>%
        transmute(
          Group    = Weather_Condition,
          N_Units  = total_accidents,
          Mean_Est = severe_percent,
          CI_Lower = lower_ci,
          CI_Upper = upper_ci,
          PI_Lower = NA_real_,
          PI_Upper = NA_real_
        )
      return(df)
    }

    monthly <- p1_monthly_variance()
    target_col <- ifelse(input$p1_ci_type == "CIPI", "severe_ratio", "severe_rate")
    upper_cap  <- ifelse(input$p1_ci_type == "CIPI", Inf, 1.0)

    res <- monthly %>%
      group_by(census_name) %>%
      summarise(
        pop      = first(population),
        N_Units  = sum(!is.na(.data[[target_col]])),
        Mean_Est = mean(.data[[target_col]], na.rm = TRUE),
        variance = var(.data[[target_col]], na.rm = TRUE),
        stdev    = sqrt(variance),
        SE       = stdev / sqrt(N_Units),
        t_val    = ifelse(N_Units > 1, qt(0.975, df = N_Units - 1), NA_real_),
        # Clamp lower bounds at 0 and rate upper bounds at 1.0
        CI_Lower = pmax(0, Mean_Est - (t_val * SE)),
        CI_Upper = pmin(upper_cap, Mean_Est + (t_val * SE)),
        PI_Lower = pmax(0, Mean_Est - (t_val * stdev * sqrt(1 + (1 / N_Units)))),
        PI_Upper = pmin(upper_cap, Mean_Est + (t_val * stdev * sqrt(1 + (1 / N_Units)))),
        .groups  = "drop"
      ) %>%
      arrange(desc(pop))

    if (input$p1_pop_tier == "all") {
      res <- res %>% slice_head(n = 15)
    }

    res %>% rename(Group = census_name)
  })

  output$p1_ci_plot <- renderPlotly({
    df <- p1_ci_data()
    validate(need(nrow(df) > 0, "Insufficient data to compute intervals."))

    is_pct <- input$p1_ci_type %in% c("CIPIrate", "SARWC")
    y_lab  <- switch(
      input$p1_ci_type,
      "CIPI"     = "Monthly Severe Accidents per 100k Residents",
      "CIPIrate" = "Monthly Severe Accident Rate (% of Accidents)",
      "SARWC"    = "Severe Accident Rate by Weather Condition (%)"
    )

    p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = reorder(Group, Mean_Est), y = Mean_Est))

    # Plot Prediction Intervals (if applicable) as thin gray background bars
    if (input$p1_ci_type != "SARWC") {
      p <- p + geom_errorbar(
        aes(ymin = PI_Lower, ymax = PI_Upper),
        width = 0.15, color = "gray65", linewidth = 0.9
      )
    }

    p <- p +
      geom_errorbar(
        aes(ymin = CI_Lower, ymax = CI_Upper),
        width = 0, color = exec_teal, linewidth = 2.4
      ) +
      geom_point(
        aes(
          text = paste0(
            "<b>", Group, "</b><br>",
            "Estimate: ", ifelse(is_pct, percent(Mean_Est, 0.1), round(Mean_Est, 2)), "<br>",
            "95% CI: [", ifelse(is_pct, percent(CI_Lower, 0.1), round(CI_Lower, 2)), ", ",
            ifelse(is_pct, percent(CI_Upper, 0.1), round(CI_Upper, 2)), "]",
            ifelse(
              !is.na(PI_Lower),
              paste0(
                "<br>95% PI: [",
                ifelse(is_pct, percent(PI_Lower, 0.1), round(PI_Lower, 2)), ", ",
                ifelse(is_pct, percent(PI_Upper, 0.1), round(PI_Upper, 2)), "]"
              ),
              ""
            )
          )
        ),
        color = exec_crimson, size = 3.2
      ) +
      coord_flip() +
      labs(x = NULL, y = y_lab) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
      theme(axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"))

    if (is_pct) {
      p <- p + scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format())
    } else {
      p <- p + scale_y_continuous(labels = comma_format())
    }

    ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text") %>%
      config(displayModeBar = FALSE)
  })

  output$p1_ci_table <- renderDT({
    df <- p1_ci_data()
    is_pct <- input$p1_ci_type %in% c("CIPIrate", "SARWC")

    tbl <- df %>%
      select(Group, N_Units, Mean_Est, CI_Lower, CI_Upper, PI_Lower, PI_Upper)

    dt <- datatable(
      tbl,
      rownames = FALSE,
      colnames = c("Locality / Condition", "N (Months/Acc)", "Mean", "95% CI Low", "95% CI High", "95% PI Low", "95% PI High"),
      options = list(pageLength = 8, dom = "tip", scrollX = TRUE)
    )

    if (is_pct) {
      dt <- dt %>% formatPercentage(c("Mean_Est", "CI_Lower", "CI_Upper", "PI_Lower", "PI_Upper"), digits = 1)
    } else {
      dt <- dt %>% formatRound(c("Mean_Est", "CI_Lower", "CI_Upper", "PI_Lower", "PI_Upper"), digits = 2)
    }
    dt
  })

  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # PAGE 2 REACTIVE DATA: COUNTY DEEP-DIVE
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  p2_county_acc <- reactive({
    acc %>% filter(census_name == input$p2_county)
  })

  output$p2_ts_title <- renderText({
    paste0("Monthly Severe Accidents & 95% Confidence Band: ", input$p2_county)
  })

  output$p2_weather_title <- renderText({
    paste0("Top Weather Conditions Associated with Severe Accidents: ", input$p2_county)
  })

  # Page 2 Plot 1: Monthly Time Series with Exact 95% CIs
  output$p2_ts_plot <- renderPlotly({
    df <- p2_county_acc() %>% filter(!is.na(month_year))
    validate(need(nrow(df) > 0, "No time-series data available for this locality."))

    all_months <- seq(min(df$month_year), max(df$month_year), by = "1 month")

    ts_df <- df %>%
      group_by(month_year) %>%
      summarise(
        total_accidents  = n(),
        severe_accidents = sum(severe, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      complete(month_year = all_months, fill = list(total_accidents = 0L, severe_accidents = 0L)) %>%
      mutate(
        # Exact 95% Poisson CI for monthly counts
        pois_low  = calc_poisson_ci(severe_accidents, "lower"),
        pois_high = calc_poisson_ci(severe_accidents, "upper"),
        # Exact 95% Binomial CI for monthly severe rate
        severe_rate = ifelse(total_accidents > 0, severe_accidents / total_accidents, NA_real_),
        rate_low    = calc_binom_ci(severe_accidents, total_accidents, "lower"),
        rate_high   = calc_binom_ci(severe_accidents, total_accidents, "upper")
      )

    if (input$p2_ts_metric == "count") {
      p <- ggplot(ts_df, aes(x = month_year, y = severe_accidents)) +
        geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pois_low, ymax = pois_high), fill = exec_teal, alpha = 0.25) +
        geom_line(color = exec_navy, linewidth = 0.9) +
        geom_point(
          aes(
            text = paste0(
              "<b>", format(month_year, "%b %Y"), "</b><br>",
              "Severe Accidents: ", comma(severe_accidents), "<br>",
              "95% Poisson CI: [", round(pois_low, 1), ", ", round(pois_high, 1), "]<br>",
              "Total Accidents: ", comma(total_accidents)
            )
          ),
          color = exec_crimson, size = 1.8
        ) +
        labs(x = "Month", y = "Number of Severe Accidents")
    } else {
      ts_valid <- ts_df %>% filter(!is.na(severe_rate))
      p <- ggplot(ts_valid, aes(x = month_year, y = severe_rate)) +
        geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = rate_low, ymax = rate_high), fill = exec_amber, alpha = 0.22) +
        geom_line(color = exec_navy, linewidth = 0.9) +
        geom_point(
          aes(
            text = paste0(
              "<b>", format(month_year, "%b %Y"), "</b><br>",
              "Severe Rate: ", percent(severe_rate, accuracy = 0.1), "<br>",
              "95% Binomial CI: [", percent(rate_low, 0.1), ", ", percent(rate_high, 0.1), "]<br>",
              "Severe / Total: ", severe_accidents, " / ", total_accidents
            )
          ),
          color = exec_crimson, size = 1.8
        ) +
        scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
        labs(x = "Month", y = "Severe Accident Rate (% of Monthly Accidents)")
    }

    p <- p +
      scale_x_datetime(date_labels = "%b %Y", date_breaks = "6 months") +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

    ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text") %>%
      config(displayModeBar = FALSE)
  })

  # Page 2 Plot 2: Worst Weather Conditions for Selected County (Plot b)
  p2_weather_data <- reactive({
    df <- p2_county_acc() %>%
      filter(!is.na(Weather_Condition), Weather_Condition != "") %>%
      group_by(Weather_Condition) %>%
      summarise(
        accidents            = n(),
        severe_accidents     = sum(severe, na.rm = TRUE),
        not_severe_accidents = sum(!severe, na.rm = TRUE),
        population           = first(population),
        severe_ratio         = (severe_accidents / population) * 100000,
        severe_rate          = severe_accidents / accidents,
        not_severe_rate      = not_severe_accidents / accidents,
        rate_ci_low          = calc_binom_ci(severe_accidents, accidents, "lower"),
        rate_ci_high         = calc_binom_ci(severe_accidents, accidents, "upper"),
        .groups = "drop"
      )
    df
  })

  output$p2_weather_plot <- renderPlotly({
    df <- p2_weather_data() %>%
      filter(accidents >= input$p2_min_weather_n) %>%
      slice_max(.data[[input$p2_weather_metric]], n = 8)

    validate(
      need(nrow(df) > 0, "No weather conditions in this locality meet the minimum accident threshold. Lower the slider on the left.")
    )

    is_rate <- input$p2_weather_metric == "severe_rate"
    y_lab   <- ifelse(
      is_rate,
      "Severe Accident Rate (% of Weather Accidents)",
      "Severe Accidents per 100,000 Residents (Severe Ratio)"
    )

    p <- ggplot(
      df,
      aes(
        x = reorder(Weather_Condition, .data[[input$p2_weather_metric]]),
        y = .data[[input$p2_weather_metric]],
        text = paste0(
          "<b>", Weather_Condition, "</b><br>",
          "Severe Rate: ", percent(severe_rate, accuracy = 0.1),
          " (95% CI: ", percent(rate_ci_low, 0.1), "–", percent(rate_ci_high, 0.1), ")<br>",
          "Severe Ratio (per 100k): ", round(severe_ratio, 2), "<br>",
          "Severe Accidents: ", comma(severe_accidents), "<br>",
          "Total Accidents: ", comma(accidents)
        )
      )
    ) +
      geom_col(fill = "#483D8B", alpha = 0.9, width = 0.65)

    if (is_rate) {
      p <- p +
        geom_errorbar(
          aes(ymin = rate_ci_low, ymax = rate_ci_high),
          width = 0.22, color = exec_amber, linewidth = 0.8
        ) +
        scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format())
    } else {
      p <- p + scale_y_continuous(labels = comma_format())
    }

    p <- p +
      coord_flip() +
      labs(x = NULL, y = y_lab) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
      theme(axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"))

    ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text") %>%
      config(displayModeBar = FALSE)
  })

  # Page 2 Table: Complete Breakdown of Rates & Counts
  output$p2_summary_table <- renderDT({
    df <- p2_weather_data() %>%
      arrange(desc(severe_accidents)) %>%
      select(
        Weather_Condition, accidents, severe_accidents, not_severe_accidents,
        severe_rate, rate_ci_low, rate_ci_high, severe_ratio
      )

    datatable(
      df,
      rownames = FALSE,
      colnames = c(
        "Weather Condition", "Total Accidents", "Severe Accidents",
        "Non-Severe Accidents", "Severe Rate (%)", "95% CI Low",
        "95% CI High", "Severe Ratio (per 100k)"
      ),
      options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE)
    ) %>%
      formatPercentage(c("severe_rate", "rate_ci_low", "rate_ci_high"), digits = 1) %>%
      formatRound("severe_ratio", digits = 2) %>%
      formatCurrency(c("accidents", "severe_accidents", "not_severe_accidents"), currency = "", interval = 3, mark = ",", digits = 0)
  })

  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # PAGE 3 REACTIVE DATA: GEOSPATIAL & STREET HOTSPOTS
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  p3_county_acc <- reactive({
    acc %>%
      filter(
        census_name == input$p3_county,
        !is.na(Start_Lat),
        !is.na(Start_Lng)
      )
  })

  # Street-level aggregation for Page 3
  p3_street_summary <- reactive({
    df <- p3_county_acc() %>%
      filter(!is.na(Street), Street != "") %>%
      group_by(Street) %>%
      summarise(
        total_accidents  = n(),
        severe_accidents = sum(severe, na.rm = TRUE),
        population       = first(population),
        severe_rate      = severe_accidents / total_accidents,
        severe_ratio     = (severe_accidents / population) * 100000,
        rate_ci_low      = calc_binom_ci(severe_accidents, total_accidents, "lower"),
        rate_ci_high     = calc_binom_ci(severe_accidents, total_accidents, "upper"),
        lat              = median(Start_Lat, na.rm = TRUE),
        lng              = median(Start_Lng, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      filter(total_accidents >= input$p3_min_street_n) %>%
      arrange(desc(.data[[input$p3_street_metric]]), desc(total_accidents))

    df
  })

  output$p3_map_title <- renderText({
    paste0("Geospatial Street Hotspot Map: ", input$p3_county)
  })

  output$p3_map <- renderLeaflet({
    df_pts <- p3_county_acc()
    validate(need(nrow(df_pts) > 0, "No geocoded accident records found for this locality."))

    # Match boundary via exact 5-digit Census GEOID (avoids Fairfax County vs. Fairfax city collision)
    target_geoid <- unique(df_pts$GEOID)[1]
    boundary_poly <- NULL
    if (!is.null(va_boundaries) && !is.na(target_geoid)) {
      boundary_poly <- va_boundaries %>% filter(GEOID == target_geoid)
    }

    m <- leaflet() %>%
      addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron)

    if (!is.null(boundary_poly) && nrow(boundary_poly) > 0) {
      m <- m %>%
        addPolygons(
          data = boundary_poly,
          fill = TRUE,
          fillColor = exec_navy,
          fillOpacity = 0.05,
          color = exec_navy,
          weight = 3,
          opacity = 0.9,
          group = "County Boundary"
        )
    }

    if (input$p3_map_mode == "streets") {
      streets_df <- p3_street_summary() %>%
        slice_head(n = input$p3_top_n_streets)

      validate(
        need(nrow(streets_df) > 0, "No streets meet the minimum accident threshold. Lower the 'Min. Total Accidents on Street' slider.")
      )

      pal <- colorNumeric(
        palette = "plasma",
        domain = streets_df[[input$p3_street_metric]],
        reverse = TRUE
      )

      # Scale marker radius smoothly between 6 and 20 pixels based on total accidents on street
      max_acc <- max(streets_df$total_accidents, 1)
      radii   <- 6 + 14 * sqrt(streets_df$total_accidents / max_acc)

      m <- m %>%
        addCircleMarkers(
          data = streets_df,
          lng = ~lng,
          lat = ~lat,
          radius = radii,
          fillColor = ~pal(streets_df[[input$p3_street_metric]]),
          color = "#1A202C",
          weight = 1.2,
          fillOpacity = 0.85,
          popup = ~paste0(
            "<b>Street: </b>", Street, "<br>",
            "<b>Locality: </b>", input$p3_county, "<br>",
            "<b>Severe Accidents: </b>", comma(severe_accidents), "<br>",
            "<b>Total Accidents: </b>", comma(total_accidents), "<br>",
            "<b>Severe Rate: </b>", percent(severe_rate, accuracy = 0.1),
            " (95% CI: ", percent(rate_ci_low, 0.1), "–", percent(rate_ci_high, 0.1), ")<br>",
            "<b>Severe Ratio (per 100k): </b>", round(severe_ratio, 2)
          )
        ) %>%
        addLegend(
          position = "bottomright",
          pal = pal,
          values = streets_df[[input$p3_street_metric]],
          title = switch(
            input$p3_street_metric,
            "severe_accidents" = "Severe Count",
            "severe_rate"      = "Severe Rate",
            "severe_ratio"     = "Severe / 100k"
          ),
          opacity = 0.85
        )
    } else {
      # Individual severe accident points (capped at 2,500 points for smooth browser rendering)
      sev_pts <- df_pts %>%
        filter(severe) %>%
        slice_head(n = 2500)

      validate(need(nrow(sev_pts) > 0, "No severe accidents recorded in this locality."))

      m <- m %>%
        addCircleMarkers(
          data = sev_pts,
          lng = ~Start_Lng,
          lat = ~Start_Lat,
          radius = 4,
          color = exec_crimson,
          fillOpacity = 0.65,
          stroke = FALSE,
          popup = ~paste0(
            "<b>Street: </b>", Street, "<br>",
            "<b>Severity: </b>", Severity, "<br>",
            "<b>Weather: </b>", Weather_Condition, "<br>",
            "<b>Time: </b>", Start_Time
          )
        )
    }

    m
  })

  output$p3_street_table <- renderDT({
    df <- p3_street_summary() %>%
      select(
        Street, total_accidents, severe_accidents,
        severe_rate, rate_ci_low, rate_ci_high, severe_ratio
      )

    datatable(
      df,
      rownames = FALSE,
      colnames = c(
        "Street / Highway", "Total Acc.", "Severe Acc.",
        "Severe Rate (%)", "95% CI Low", "95% CI High", "Severe per 100k"
      ),
      options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE)
    ) %>%
      formatPercentage(c("severe_rate", "rate_ci_low", "rate_ci_high"), digits = 1) %>%
      formatRound("severe_ratio", digits = 2)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

## 4. Chronological Record of Human Verification Checks & Revisions

### Verification Check & Revision 1: Perceptual Clutter of Bar-Chart Error Bars & Multiplicity Correction

- **Human Prompt / Audit Observation (11/10/2026):**
  - *"on the first page, the CIs that are on page 1 in black and are layered on the bar chart seem to crowd the perspective way too much. Is there a reason why that is?"*
  - *"In general, all CIs and PIs should be kept as a separate dedicated chart and not combined in a bar chart. So yes, remove the error bars from the top row bar charts in both page 1 and page 2. Adjust PI and CI charts to also account for multiple comparisons. Finally, add a CI PI chart for page 2. Output the full corrected app code."*
- **What Our Verification Established (Defect Found & Corrected):**
  1.  **Perceptual & Statistical Defect:** Ranking rare weather conditions by highest severity percentage (`slice_max(severe_percent, n = 10)`) surfaced low-denominator weather events ($n = 20\text{–}35$ accidents) whose exact 95% Clopper-Pearson binomial intervals spanned $30\text{–}45$ percentage points. Layering `geom_errorbar(width = 0.25)` onto solid `geom_col()` bars in `ggplotly()` created competing visual boundaries and heavy vertical end-cap clutter ("picket fence" effect), duplicating the dedicated uncertainty card below it.
  2.  **Unadjusted Multiplicity Risk:** Comparing $m = 5$ to $15$ counties or $m = 10$ weather conditions simultaneously at marginal $\alpha = 0.05$ inflated the Family-Wise Error Rate ($\text{FWER} = 1 - (1 - 0.05)^m \approx 40.1\%$ for $m = 10$).
- **Human Revision Applied:**
  - Removed `geom_errorbar()` from all top-row bar charts (`p1_county_plot`, `p1_weather_plot`, and `p2_weather_plot`).
  - Added a dedicated interval card on Page 2 (`p2_ci_plot` and `p2_ci_table`).
  - Implemented `get_adjusted_alpha()` supporting **Bonferroni** ($\alpha_{\text{adj}} = \alpha / m$) and **Šidák** ($\alpha_{\text{adj}} = 1 - (1 - \alpha)^{1/m}$) simultaneous adjustments across $m$ groups.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Verification Check & Revision 2: Geospatial Map Blank-Screen Failure on Page 3

- **Human Prompt / Audit Observation (11/10/2026):**
  - *"whats wrong with the map? it doesn't show Virginia as a whole when I click on individual counties, the map basically reads blank. It would be better if it was like a real map. can you help me figure out what to do?"*
- **What Our Verification Established (Defect Found & Corrected):**
  1.  **Silent Blank-Map Failure on Rural Counties:** In `output$p3_map`, filtering streets by `total_accidents >= 5` followed by `validate(need(nrow(streets_df) > 0, ...))` caused `renderLeaflet()` to abort completely and wipe the entire map canvas blank whenever a rural Virginia county had fewer than 5 accidents on any single street.
  2.  **Loss of Statewide Context:** Filtering `va_boundaries` to only the single selected `GEOID` deleted the other 132 Virginia counties from the map.
  3.  **Featureless Basemap & Unbounded Zoom:** `CartoDB.Positron` tiles lacked visible road networks, and without `fitBounds()` locked to the official Census polygon, stray GPS coordinates pulled the map camera into blank space.
- **Human Revision Applied:**
  - Permanently rendered all 133 Virginia counties/cities as a clickable choropleth background layer shaded by `severe_ratio`.
  - Switched default map tiles to **OpenStreetMap (Road Map)** with layer toggles for **Esri World Street Map** and **Esri Satellite Imagery**.
  - Added an automatic fallback in `p3_street_summary()` so if `0` streets meet the slider threshold in a rural county, it falls back to all geocoded streets (`min = 1`) rather than blanking the map.
  - Locked the camera bounding box (`fitBounds()`) to the selected county's `tigris` Census polygon and added a `"Zoom Out to Full Virginia Map"` button.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Verification Check & Revision 3: Degrees-of-Freedom ($\text{df}$) Starvation in Page 2 Weather Intervals

- **Human Prompt / Audit Observation (11/10/2026):**
  - *"why on page 2 do the CI's and PI's seem too large. for example the Heavy T-Storm / Windy one is 0 - 100% for both"*
  - *"so the idea is extreme weather conditions don't have a lot of months where the weather condition occurred at sufficient rate in the month? so there is essentially not enough df?"*
- **What Our Verification Established (Defect Found & Corrected):**
  - When slicing a single county simultaneously by month (`month_year`) and by 73 granular NOAA weather strings, hyper-specific storm labels like `"Heavy T-Storm / Windy"` occurred in only $N = 2$ or $N = 3$ distinct calendar months over the 7-year span (with $0$ accidents in the other $\sim 82$ months, which are `NA` for conditional severity rates).
  - With $N = 2$ or $3$ active months, the degrees of freedom collapsed to $\text{df} = N - 1 = 1$ or $2$. Under a Bonferroni adjustment across $m = 8$ weather conditions ($\alpha_{\text{adj}} = 0.00625$), the Student's $t$ critical value `qt(1 - 0.00625/2, df)` exploded to $12.64$ ($\text{df} = 2$) and $101.81$ ($\text{df} = 1$).
  - Combined with 1-accident months that could only take binary $0\%$ or $100\%$ rates ($s \approx 57.7\%$), the margin of error exceeded $\pm 400\%$ and clipped to `[0.0%, 100.0%]`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Verification Check & Revision 4: Auditing One-Sided Logit CIs & Enforcing Executive Simplicity

- **Human Prompt / Audit Observation (11/10/2026):**
  - *"I'm trying to have the graph look at given the county, given the weather condition, the monthly variability in given accident rate or ratio. whats the best solution for that? State the best solution first before outputting any code"*
  - *"this looks better but is it a problem that some of the CIs look like they are only on side?"*
  - *"I don't want to make the interpretation of the confidence intervals on page 2 too complicated for the average viewer. Can you come up with the simplest way to change it so that the explanation is clear, simple, the CIs don't cover 100% of the graph, and each CI has enough of an n to mean something?"*
- **What Our Verification Established (Defect Found & Corrected):**
  - **One-Sided CI Defect in Logit Continuity Correction:** The AI's intermediate fix used an empirical logit transformation $\eta_t = \ln\left(\frac{k_t + 0.5}{n_t - k_t + 0.5}\right)$ for the interval bounds while plotting the true pooled proportion $\hat{p} = \frac{\sum k_t}{\sum n_t}$ as the red dot. Adding `+ 0.5` to small monthly counts pulled `inv_logit(eta_bar)` toward $50\%$, shifting the entire confidence interval to the right of the red dot so the interval appeared one-sided!
  - **Human Statistical & Design Judgment:** Rather than patching a complex Delta-method logit transformation that would be difficult to explain to the Governor's Office, we established three transparent data rules that keep the standard textbook formula ($\text{Mean} \pm t_{\text{adj}, \, n-1} \cdot \text{SE}$):
    1.  Group the 73 fragmented weather strings into **5 Core Weather Categories** (*Clear / Fair*, *Cloudy / Overcast*, *Light-Moderate Rain / Drizzle*, *Thunderstorms / Heavy Rain*, and *Snow / Ice / Fog*).
    2.  Require at least **5 accidents in a month** (`accidents >= 5`) for that month to count as a valid monthly observation (eliminating binary $0\%/100\%$ single-accident noise).
    3.  Require at least $n \ge 10$ qualifying months ($\text{df} \ge 9$) per weather bar so $t$-critical values stay well-behaved ($\le 3.25$) and every red dot is strictly centered inside its confidence interval.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Verification Check & Revision 5: Removing Uninformative Prediction Intervals (PIs) & Fixing Plotly End-Cap Collisions

- **Human Prompt / Audit Observation (11/10/2026):**
  - *"The CIs are better. In many cases though the PIs are effectively meaningless in page 1 and page 2. can you edit the CI and PI charts to remove the PI part and just focus on CI's? Also make sure the charts and tables correctly reflect the choice, if no PIs are calculated they shouldn't be in the table, the graph or the label. Make the necessary edits."*
  - *"on page 2 this change made the CI bar ends too large they are merging into other categories. Can you please regenerate the code with this fix?"*
- **What Our Verification Established (Defect Found & Corrected):**
  1.  **Analytical Scope Pruning (Removing PIs):** Because monthly traffic crash counts and weather-conditioned rates exhibit strong seasonal variation, parametric normal/Student-$t$ Prediction Intervals ($\text{Mean} \pm t \cdot s\sqrt{1 + 1/n}$) were too wide to support county budget allocation decisions. Removing PIs across Pages 1 and 2 focused the visual hierarchy squarely on the **Simultaneous 95% Confidence Intervals for the Mean**.
  2.  **Plotly Whisker Collision Bug:** Setting `geom_errorbar(width = 0.2)` inside a `coord_flip()` chart converted by `ggplotly()` caused Plotly's SVG renderer to draw tall vertical end-caps that collided across adjacent weather rows on Page 2. Setting `width = 0` restored clean horizontal confidence interval bars.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Verification Check & Revision 6: Confidence Interval Audit

- **Human Prompt / Audit Observation (11/13/2026):**
  - *"The confidence intervals on the dashboard needed to be checked to ensure they were calculated correctly, centered around the estimates, and displayed within valid ranges."*
- **What Our Verification Established (Defect Found & Corrected):**
  1.  We added checks to confirm that each confidence interval had valid lower and upper bounds, contained its estimate, and matched the underlying calculations. Any inconsistencies were identified and corrected.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Verification Check & Revision 7: Weather Grouping Audit

- **Human Prompt / Audit Observation (11/13/2026):**
  - *"The dashboard grouped many individual weather descriptions into broader categories. We needed to verify that the original weather conditions were assigned to the correct groups and that no accident records were lost."*
- **What Our Verification Established (Defect Found & Corrected):**
  1.  We compared the original weather descriptions with their assigned categories and checked that grouped accident counts matched the source data. Incorrect group assignments or count discrepancies were identified and corrected.

acc_raw <- read.csv(existing_path, na.strings = c("", "NA"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Group the 73 raw NOAA weather strings into 5 intuitive Weather Categories
classify_weather_simple <- function(w) {
  w_low <- str_to_lower(coalesce(w, ""))
  case_when(
    w_low == "" ~ NA_character_,
    str_detect(w_low, "t-storm|thunder|heavy rain|squall|tornado|hail") ~ "Thunderstorms / Heavy Rain",
    str_detect(w_low, "snow|sleet|ice|freezing|wintry|blizzard|fog|mist|haze") ~ "Snow / Ice / Fog",
    str_detect(w_low, "rain|drizzle|shower|precip") ~ "Light-Moderate Rain / Drizzle",
    str_detect(w_low, "cloud|overcast") ~ "Cloudy / Overcast",
    str_detect(w_low, "clear|fair") ~ "Clear / Fair",
    TRUE ~ "Other Weather"
  )
}

    Start_Time        = ymd_hms(Start_Time, tz = "UTC", quiet = TRUE),
    End_Time          = ymd_hms(End_Time, tz = "UTC", quiet = TRUE),
    Year              = year(Start_Time),
    month_year        = floor_date(Start_Time, unit = "month"),
    severe            = Severity >= 3,

    Weather_Condition = str_squish(Weather_Condition),

  ) %>%

# Pre-compute static county population & statewide accident summary for the VA map

  group_by(GEOID, census_name) %>%

    population       = first(na.omit(population)),
    total_accidents  = n(),
    severe_accidents = sum(severe, na.rm = TRUE),
    severe_rate      = ifelse(total_accidents > 0, severe_accidents / total_accidents, 0),
    severe_ratio     = (severe_accidents / population) * 100000,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(population)) %>%
  mutate(pop_rank = row_number())

n_localities <- nrow(county_pop_ranks)
mid_start    <- max(1, floor((n_localities - 5) / 2) + 1)
mid_indices  <- mid_start:min(n_localities, mid_start + 4)

middle5_pop_names <- county_pop_ranks %>% slice(mid_indices) %>% pull(census_name)
bottom5_pop_names <- county_pop_ranks %>% slice_tail(n = 5) %>% pull(census_name)

all_years    <- sort(unique(acc$Year))
all_counties <- county_pop_ranks$census_name

# Load all 133 Virginia county/city boundaries and join county summary metrics

    st_transform(4326) %>%

    mutate(
      display_name     = coalesce(census_name, NAMELSAD, NAME),
      total_accidents  = replace_na(total_accidents, 0L),
      severe_accidents = replace_na(severe_accidents, 0L),
      severe_rate      = replace_na(severe_rate, 0),
      severe_ratio     = replace_na(severe_ratio, 0)
    )
}, error = function(e) {
  NULL
})

# ==============================================================================
# SIMPLE, STANDARD STATISTICAL HELPER FUNCTIONS (CONFIDENCE INTERVALS ONLY)
# ==============================================================================
get_adjusted_alpha <- function(m, method = c("bonferroni", "sidak", "none"), alpha = 0.05) {
  method <- match.arg(method)
  m <- max(1, as.integer(m))
  switch(
    method,
    "bonferroni" = alpha / m,
    "sidak"      = 1 - (1 - alpha)^(1 / m),
    "none"       = alpha
  )
}

calc_binom_ci <- function(x, n, bound = c("lower", "upper"), conf_level = 0.95) {
  bound <- match.arg(bound)
  idx <- ifelse(bound == "lower", 1, 2)
  conf_level <- pmin(pmax(conf_level, 0.50), 0.999999)
  map2_dbl(x, n, function(k, total) {
    if (is.na(k) || is.na(total) || total <= 0) return(NA_real_)
    binom.test(k, total, conf.level = conf_level)$conf.int[idx]
  })
}

calc_poisson_ci <- function(k_vec, bound = c("lower", "upper"), conf_level = 0.95) {
  bound <- match.arg(bound)
  idx <- ifelse(bound == "lower", 1, 2)
  conf_level <- pmin(pmax(conf_level, 0.50), 0.999999)
  map_dbl(k_vec, function(k) {
    if (is.na(k) || k < 0) return(NA_real_)
    poisson.test(as.integer(round(k)), conf.level = conf_level)$conf.int[idx]
  })
}

compute_simple_ci <- function(df, group_col, value_col, pop_col = NULL,
                              mult_method = "bonferroni", upper_cap = Inf,
                              min_months = 10) {
  grouped <- df %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[value_col]]) & !is.nan(.data[[value_col]])) %>%
    group_by(Group = .data[[group_col]]) %>%
    summarise(
      pop      = if (!is.null(pop_col)) first(.data[[pop_col]]) else NA_real_,
      N_Units  = n(),
      Mean_Est = mean(.data[[value_col]], na.rm = TRUE),
      variance = var(.data[[value_col]], na.rm = TRUE),
      stdev    = sqrt(pmax(0, variance)),
      SE       = stdev / sqrt(N_Units),
      .groups  = "drop"
    ) %>%
    filter(Mean_Est > 0)

  filtered <- grouped %>% filter(N_Units >= min_months)
  if (nrow(filtered) == 0) filtered <- grouped %>% filter(N_Units >= 5)
  if (nrow(filtered) == 0) filtered <- grouped %>% filter(N_Units >= 3)

  m_groups  <- max(1, nrow(filtered))
  alpha_adj <- get_adjusted_alpha(m_groups, mult_method, alpha = 0.05)

  filtered %>%
    mutate(
      m_comparisons = m_groups,
      conf_level    = 1 - alpha_adj,
      t_val         = qt(1 - (alpha_adj / 2), df = pmax(1, N_Units - 1)),
      CI_Lower      = pmax(0, Mean_Est - (t_val * SE)),
      CI_Upper      = pmin(upper_cap, Mean_Est + (t_val * SE))
    )
}
